item.text: {"code":"","conclusion":"The recorded results show a positive SES–BA completion association: large in relative terms, but modest in absolute probability and weak in correlation. Among 8,773 respondents, 236 completed a BA (2.69%; 95% CI 2.37–3.05%). Completion rates across ascending SES quintiles were 0.68%, 2.74%, 3.13%, 3.37%, and 3.53%. The highest versus lowest quintile difference was 2.85 percentage points (95% CI 1.93–3.86), with a risk ratio of 5.17 (95% CI 2.79–9.55). The point-biserial correlation was 0.061. Unadjusted logistic regression reported an odds ratio of 1.42 per SES standard deviation (95% CI 1.27–1.59); predicted completion rose from 1.70% at the SES 10th percentile to 3.93% at the 90th, a 2.23-percentage-point difference (95% CI 1.49–2.96). All rows were analyzed, with no missing outcome, missing or invalid SES, or duplicate case IDs. Boolean false/true mapped to 0/1 consistently with the documented outcome; no indicator mismatch was apparent. Both executions succeeded. Evidence roots: analysis a3fbca7401f37e9199fad0ff54ca0b37a9d689430a72b64f5150232e072a9a53; profile e320f5a2bbf69d84def7fc25d7fdc0e6f90161c13681132c5d75b639d36fce06.","limitations":["The validator verifies execution receipts, identity, and input hash only; these scientific results are not independently validated.","These are observational, unadjusted associations and do not establish a causal effect of SES.","No survey weights, strata, or cluster identifiers were supplied; estimates describe this sample and confidence intervals assume independent respondents.","Processed-data selection and measurement limitations cannot be assessed from the supplied outputs.","SES quintiles are sample-relative, with ties retained together. Logistic regression assumes linear SES effects on log odds; its odds ratio is not a probability ratio."]}
